scope: Direct include/xsf/*.h and include/xsf/cpu/*.h; cephes, AMOS, specfun, Carlson and third_party descendants are private algorithm implementations. Header-family review is not overload/domain coverage.

groups.notes: Existing real functional APIs cover the numerical families. Float width overloads collapse into sci_core::Float; aliases and private approximation routines are not separate APIs.

Add gamma_ratio, digammainv, iv_ratio, iv_ratio_c, iv_ratioinv, scaled_exp1, normalized_gen_harmonic, and log1pmx. Complex exp1/expi/xlogy/xlog1py remain deferred; complex log1p belongs to sci::complex.

Add tested generic complex gamma/error/Bessel/Hankel/Airy/Fresnel APIs using shared Sci Complex and Result. Complex erfi/erfcx/Dawson are tested through private Faddeeva kernels with explicit series bounds, stable scaling and shared finite-input/result errors. Internal w_im and approximation dispatches stay private.

Tested generic complex digamma, analytic loggamma and entire reciprocal gamma use shared Sci Complex and Result, bounded shared expansions and stable scaled reflection. Poles return errors for digamma/loggamma and exact zeros for rgamma; signed-zero loggamma banks preserve the unwrapped phase.

Real APIs remain covered; complex Spence, bounded Riemann/Hurwitz zeta and integer Lambert W branches now have public Rust APIs with independent tests. Complex hypergeometric and Wright omega, plus zeta outside documented bounded domains, remain candidate additions. Private helpers are not counted as public coverage.
Integer degrees and recurrence evaluators are implemented; noninteger hypergeometric degree continuations are deferred. Backend _l suffixes and duplicate order/precision overloads are not exported.
Use Ellip notation, domains and Sci shared errors. Complex Carlson integrals remain deferred. Unchecked/precision-control helpers are private.

Real bounded value and sequence APIs and shared complex harmonic results exist. General complex arguments and derivative tensors remain deferred; callback, mdspan, normalization-policy and dual-number plumbing is not reproduced.

Reuse existing bounded Rust wave, integral, zero, distribution and sequence APIs; callbacks, raw output pointers, legacy argument permutations and algorithm subroutines stay private. This is family coverage, not a claim of every domain or signature.

Retain existing documented distribution functions in special. New cosine/von-Mises/Tukey-lambda, Poisson-binomial, Wilcoxon distribution tables, Cramer-von-Mises, generalized hyperbolic/inverse Gaussian densities, and multivariate normal CDFs belong to a coherent sci::stats API; missing stats operations are deferred, not counted as implemented.

Use standard float methods/constants, sci::complex arithmetic and sci::polynomials evaluation. Do not duplicate cbrt/exp2/exp10/expm1/log1p/constants or expose raw polynomial-array conventions. Cancellation-sensitive new arithmetic should be implemented in its owning module.

C++/NumPy/CuPy adapters, device configuration, layouts, dual-number internals, callback recurrence engines, low-level solvers/error hooks and test error metrics are infrastructure. Use Rust types, slices/iterators, shared Result and existing Sci algorithms. Internal numerical kernels are not public coverage targets.
